title: PR body claims palcheck floors were re-pinned; no palcheck floor changed in the diff
evidence:
_pr_body_camera_zoom_tiers.md:58: "- **palcheck floors re-pinned where the puck shrink dropped pixel counts**
  (e.g. the puck hardware-tone floor) — measured on the re-blessed frames,". harness/palcheck.odin:319 (byte-identical to parent f28fb7c, zero harness files in the commit): "check(count_near(calm, rl.Color{86, 98, 116, 255}, 12) > 200, \"puck hardware tone\", ...)". Commit message: "palcheck stays green (floors had margin) - no re-pin needed."
detail: The PR body (the declared spec) asserts a re-pin that never happened; the commit message says the opposite. Live `tools/harness.sh palcheck` passes, so the gate is green — but the spec misdescribes the change.
recommended_fix: Amend the PR body: replace the re-pinned sentence with the commit message's truth — floors had margin, palcheck stayed green, no re-pin needed.

title: camera_set_fit is now uncalled dead code
evidence: app/main.odin:1746: "camera_set_fit :: proc(app: ^App) {" — grep across app/, harness/, core/ finds zero call sites (only the definition and comments). Commit message: "camera_set_fit keeps the out-limit framing." The actual out-limit is main.odin:1991: "z_to := clamp(rnd.camera_zoom_step(app.cam_zoom_to, delta), rnd.CAM_ZOOM_MIN, rnd.CAM_ZOOM_MAX)".
detail: Demoted to non-resting, the proc lost every caller; the out-limit framing is enforced by camera_zoom_at's clamp instead. Retained 'framing' is untestable dead weight.
recommended_fix: Delete camera_set_fit (and its comment) or wire it as the documented out-limit helper; either way keep a pin that the wheel floor is CAM_ZOOM_MIN.

title: Auto-pullback never fires from the new resting home (inert at DEFAULT_ZOOM)
detail: At the resting default (zoom == 2.0), any out-of-view district floors z_to to 2.0 and returns inactive — the v2-camera-zoom auto-pullback only fires above 2.0. Documented as the accepted tradeoff; surfacing for visibility.
recommended_fix: None required — spec documents it ('or stay out'). Optionally surface new districts another way (alert/forecast) so resting players learn of distant seeds.
